instruction: ARTBOOK FIRST remains the production gate. Artbook creation, upgrades, revisions, and existing-game initial backfill have no daily or weekly count limit; serialization exists only where shared state or final integration would conflict. Every existing game without an initial artbook must be backfilled continuously until the backlog is empty, with workflow-run continuation plus watchdog recovery if the chain stops. For each game, Vibe2 authors a proposal first draft, then planning, graphics, development, QA, and balance each own and submit their specialist sections. The director/ChatGPT may assemble and summarize submitted sections but may not invent missing specialist content. An approved artbook is a living versioned game design baseline, not a one-time terminal deliverable: DESIGN_BASELINE is used for development, development-confirmed requires a DEVELOPMENT_BASELINE upgrade, release-confirmed requires a RELEASE_BASELINE upgrade, and QA/playtest/balance/story/technical/content findings may request a new revision at any time without overwriting history. When a development-confirmed game's DESIGN_BASELINE is completed, that game enters the development scoring queue; completion no longer guarantees immediate deep-development execution. Deep development is limited to at most two focused games company-wide. Focus is scored on five 0-2 axes: playability, distinctiveness, development efficiency, scalability, and low blockage. The highest scoring eligible games occupy the two focus slots, with existing Unity winning a same-score tie; a dedicated Unity-primary project still consumes one focus slot even when its execution uses a separate Unity lane. Non-focused development-confirmed games stay in next-development and may receive planning, artbook, analysis, or FAST maintenance without consuming a deep-development slot. Focus is reevaluated after a material milestone, two consecutive floors without meaningful progress, a structural/dependency block, a higher-score candidate, or release readiness. Runtime incidents use a lightweight FAST lane: development and QA perform the substantive pre-fix review, development owns the code modification, independent browser/final QA and the existing release gate remain mandatory, and unrelated planning/graphics/balance AI work is skipped. Release-confirmed stable games do not receive arbitrary feature development and enter FAST only when an actual runtime incident exists. Vibe2 is the company-wide production/analysis/verification engine, and department AIs use and correct its capabilities throughout design, implementation, graphics, QA, balance and learning; Vibe output is not authoritative until department evidence and required QA validate it. During a normal autonomous floor, the five departments review in parallel. Planning owns final integration constraints and file ownership; development, graphics, QA and balance may modify disjoint owned code scopes in isolated parallel workspaces. NO_SCOPE is a normal result when a department has no disjoint responsibility file for that floor. Non-conflicting department changes are integrated automatically from the common baseline, true same-file conflicts require explicit conflict resolution, and only the final integrated candidate proceeds to one strong independent QA/promotion gate. Source workers never write main directly. Verified candidates may promote only through the existing release gate, followed by public health/runtime verification; verified success/failure evidence is fed into existing Company DNA/Vibe learning and may trigger an Artbook revision or baseline upgrade before the next development floor. Release-confirmed critical runtime incidents may preempt ordinary work for stability protection. The director is the company's active staff supervisor and operational bottleneck resolver: owner-immediate instructions are always first, then release safety, focused deep development, next-development maintenance/planning, structure-improvement, planning/identity, reviewing/other and HOLD. For every department the director verifies actual task assignment, workflow/execution evidence, result evidence, verification, blockers and next action. A running label without execution evidence is not work and must be classified as FALSE_RUNNING or STALE. When assigned work is not progressing, the director must identify whether the cause is a missing work order, missing or untriggered automation, workflow failure, missing output, validation failure, dependency/permission problem, evidence-adapter mismatch, stale queue or stopped backfill/development chain. The director may fix low-risk operational blockers, re-dispatch stopped approved workflows, and reapply owner priority when no conflicting active run exists; it must not ghostwrite specialist output, bypass QA, change locked game concepts, use paid services, or decide core owner-gated changes. Homepage exposure is not itself a production-approval gate. Artbooks remain game-specific and follow artbook-style-profiles.json; uniform templates are forbidden. Story causality is the highest quality gate. Unity Android test builds use the verified hybrid build route and build success requires a non-empty APK plus SHA-256. After any material implementation, build, gameplay, graphics, QA, or balance modification, previous department votes must not be carried forward as the post-change verdict. Once current verification evidence exists, planning, development, QA, graphics, and balance must independently reevaluate the modified state, then the director must aggregate only those five submitted reviews and cast a new PASS/REVISE/DROP verdict. Within the same release state, existing Unity games come first, existing Web maintenance second, new Unity third, then other engines. Existing Web games may receive low-risk bug fixes, mobile UI/UX, accessibility, performance, structural cleanup, and regression fixes. New Web game production is not the default target and core gameplay, balance, save meaning, and major content direction still require owner decisions. Automatic Play Store publication is not implied by test APK prerelease. Never use paid automation or paid runners.
